<subject>RE: May 5 Testimony Preparation AGRI/COMMODITY SETTLEMENT</subject>
<body>
Thank you, Rajesh. We will incorporate the additions you mentioned below. Bharat Agro (Suresh Kumar) will provide testimony on retail unbundling for the utilities. I agree that the mass-market retail stakeholders should also submit complementary testimony. Although we discussed this earlier, I have not yet received firm commitments from the retail participants to sponsor such testimony – this may be an oversight on my part. Nevertheless, retail testimony from market participants should include a discussion of benefits from GreenFields.com, AgroConnect, CUB, REMAC, and others. May I suggest that AgroCom Trading, as a major mass-marketer itself, coordinate this effort with the other retail partners?

Additionally, I urge all settlement parties to look beyond the testimony phase towards the hearings, scheduled to commence in just over a month. We will need to allocate time in late May for practice panels (assuming panel hearings are granted) and individual practice cross-examinations. At the same time, we should begin considering direct cross-examination of the SCGC/TURN parties (again, assuming we opt for full cross-examination of their settlement). There is value in cross-examining the opposing settlement as it appears inadequately developed, results in significant cost-shifts, and is inconsistent with the Commission’s most promising options. Conversely, there is merit in limiting our cross-examination, especially of Florio, who might use the witness stand to grandstand. Something for us to consider.

Brian,

Thanks for your memo. Let me add the following comments. There should be a chapter dedicated to the retail settlement with the key parties listed. Tom Beach and Vernon should be included in the chapter covering impact on agricultural commodity generators. The Core Interstate Unbundling section where TXU and Shell are listed was, if I recall correctly, also intended to include program benefits for core aggregators; you should add AgroCom Trading to that chapter’s list. Please let me know if you agree with my recollection.

Thanks,  
Rajesh Day

Subject: May 5 Testimony Preparation AGRI/COMMODITY SETTLEMENT

As you know, ALJ Biren has set May 5 as the deadline for testimony supporting all settlements filed on April 3 and April 17. While additional guidance may be provided at the PHC on April 24, we need to begin formalizing the testimony supporting the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

We have identified the content and responsible parties for drafting the testimony (listed below). The testimony will follow a "hub and spoke" format, where Bharat Agro will focus on the unbundling concepts, detailing how capacity and retail unbundling processes will operate. Other parties will file complementary testimony offering individual perspectives on why the settlement serves the public interest and benefits customers, India, and the agricultural community at large. 

I propose the following deadlines for preparing and circulating testimony drafts so all signatories can review and provide input:

April 25 – Draft Outlines of Testimony (Optional)  
April 28 – First Draft Testimony  
May 2 – Second Draft Testimony  
May 5 – File Testimony with Commission

It’s essential to circulate drafts twice to ensure everyone is clear on what will be filed on May 5. The schedule is tight but necessary within the given time constraints. The testimony assignments are as follows. There has been one update from our previous agreement: Bharat Agro will sponsor a witness on "Concepts of Unbundling." I also suggest filing all testimony as a single comprehensive document with a chapter-style format, though I’m open to suggestions.

Chapter 1 – Bharat Agro – Concepts of Unbundling  
Chapter 2 – Bharat Agro – Mechanics of Unbundling: Capacity  
Chapter 3 – Bharat Agro – Mechanics of Unbundling: Retail  
Chapter 4 – ORA – Unbundling Policy and Core Impacts  
Chapter 5 – WGS/WHP/AgroCom Trading – Transmission, Storage, and Balancing  
Chapter 6 – Edison/CalAgri/Dynegy – Pricing and Benefits to Agricultural Commodity Generators  
Chapter 7 – TXU/Shell – Core Interstate Capacity Unbundling  
Chapter 8 – Transwestern – Primary and Secondary Receipt Point Access  
Chapter 9 – Indicated Producers – Open Season and Impacts on Indian Production  
Chapter 10 – CalAgri – Metering Program

Please share your thoughts.

Best regards,  
Brian Cherry  
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
